title: Unit 2 Final Paper Exam: Nonlinear Functions
subtitle: Standards W2 & W3 · 15 Questions · ~60 min · Print & Write
purpose: Final paper exam before Wednesday retake. All new numbers. Matches baseline exam structure exactly. Paper-administered: Kai writes answers by hand. Special focus on Q11 (fractional exponents — the one miss from RP4).

questions.rationale: Confidence builder. Kai is 3/3 on quadratic identify across RP3 and RP4. New coefficient and numbers. Locks in the pattern before harder questions.
questions.question_html: Identify the parent function and find the x-intercepts: \( f(x) = 3(x - 4)^2 - 75 \)
questions.hint: Set f(x)=0. Isolate the squared term. Then take ±√.
solution_steps: Parent: y = x² (quadratic — highest power is 2).

questions.rationale: Kai is 2/2 on square root identify. New shift values. Keeps the pattern: isolate the radical, square, solve.
questions.question_html: Identify the parent function and find the x-intercept: \( f(x) = \sqrt{x - 11} - 6 \)
questions.hint: Set f(x)=0. Isolate the √. Square both sides.
questions.feedback_correct: Square root identified and intercept correct.
questions.feedback_wrong: Parent: square root. Isolate the √: √(x−11)=6 → x−11=36 → x=47.

questions.rationale: Absolute value with factor-out step. Kai is 2/2 on this type. New values for a, h, k. Requires the two-case split — reinforcing the most conceptually important step in W2.b.
questions.question_html: For \( f(x) = |4x - 12| - 8 \): rewrite in the form \( a|x - h| + k \), state the parent function, identify a, h, k, and find the x-intercepts.

inputs.label: Write the two equations you must solve (e.g. "AX+B = k and AX+B = -k")

questions.hint: Factor out the coefficient first. Then two cases: 4x−12=8 OR −(4x−12)=8.
solution_steps: a = 4 (vertical stretch ×4), h = 3 (shift right 3), k = −8 (shift down 8).
KEY: |A| = k means A = k OR −A = k. So: 4x−12 = 8 AND −(4x−12) = 8.
questions.feedback_correct: Absolute value factored, both intercepts found.
questions.feedback_wrong: Factor out 4: 4|x−3|−8. Set |x−3|=2. Two cases: x−3=2 → x=5, x−3=−2 → x=1.

questions.rationale: Kai is 2/2 on exponential same-base equations. New base (4), new target (256=4^4). Reinforces the pattern: convert, match bases, set exponents equal.
questions.hint: Rewrite 256 as 4^?. Then set exponents equal.

questions.rationale: Kai is 2/2 on standard-form quadratic factoring. New values (product=−35, sum=+2). Keeps the same factoring technique, different sign combination.
questions.hint: Standard form. Find two numbers: product = −35, sum = +2. Factor.
solution_steps: Need two numbers: product = −35, sum = +2. Those are: +7 and −5.
questions.feedback_wrong: Standard form: (x+7)(x−5)=0. Roots: x=−7 and x=5.

questions.rationale: Kai is 4/4 on radical equations. New values. Same pattern: isolate √, square, solve, check.
questions.hint: Isolate the √ first. Then square both sides.

questions.rationale: Kai is 2/2 on mixed-base exponential (common base conversion). New bases: 4 and 32 (both powers of 2). Slightly harder because 32=2^5 and 4=2^2 require an extra conversion step.
questions.hint: Rewrite both sides as powers of 2. 4 = 2² and 32 = 2⁵.
questions.feedback_correct: Common base found. Both sides converted to base 2.
questions.feedback_wrong: Both 4 and 32 are powers of 2. Rewrite: 4=2^2 and 32=2^5.

questions.rationale: Kai is 2/2 on rational equations. New numerator and denominator. Same technique: multiply both sides by the denominator.
Radical with coefficient in front of the square root. Kai is 2/2 on this type. New values. Critical step: divide the coefficient BEFORE squaring.
questions.hint: There is a coefficient 4 in front of the √. Subtract 2, then divide by 4, THEN square.
questions.feedback_wrong: Subtract 2 first, then divide by 4 to isolate √, THEN square.

questions.rationale: Extraneous solutions — Kai is 2/2 but this is always the hardest conceptual question. New equation, same structure: radical = linear. One root will fail the check. Must check both.
questions.hint: Square both sides. You will get a quadratic. Factor it. Check BOTH answers in the original equation.
questions.feedback_correct: Caught the extraneous solution. x=7 is the only valid answer.
questions.feedback_wrong: Square both sides: x^2−7x=0 → x=0 or x=7. Check both: x=0 fails (√4≠−2).

questions.rationale: THE CRITICAL QUESTION. Kai missed this in RP4 (2x^(3/2)−14=672). Same type, new numbers designed for a clean answer: x^(3/2)=125 → x=25. The cube root of 125 is a recognizable number (5). This gives Kai a stepping stone rather than a blind calculation. Rationale: if Kai sees 125 and thinks of 5^3, the path to x=25 is clear.
questions.hint: Step 1: Get x^(3/2) alone. Step 2: Raise BOTH SIDES to the 2/3 power (flip the fraction). Step 3: ∛125 = 5, then 5² = 25.
solution_steps: Raise both sides to the 2/3 power: x = 125^(2/3).
questions.feedback_wrong: Isolate x^(3/2)=125. Then apply 2/3 power: first ∛125=5, then 5²=25.

questions.rationale: Kai is 2/2 on vertex graphing. NEW TWIST: negative leading coefficient (parabola opens DOWN). This is a deliberate difficulty bump — Kai must notice the negative sign and flip the parabola.
questions.question_html: Graph \( f(x) = -(x + 2)^2 + 9 \). State the vertex and the direction the parabola opens.
questions.hint: Vertex form: a(x−h)²+k. Vertex is (h, k). Negative a means opens DOWN.
solution_steps: Vertex form: −(x+2)²+9 → vertex at (−2, 9). a = −1 (negative → opens DOWN).
questions.feedback_correct: Vertex, direction, and graph all correct.
questions.feedback_wrong: Vertex is (h, k) = (−2, 9). Negative a means OPENS DOWN — inverted parabola.

questions.rationale: Kai is 2/2 on rational function graphing. New shifts (right 3, down 2) with a positive multiplier. Same technique: VA from denominator, HA from shift outside.
questions.question_html: Graph \( f(x) = \dfrac{4}{x - 3} - 2 \) and draw asymptotes. State the asymptotes.
questions.hint: VA: set denominator = 0. HA: the −2 outside the fraction.
solution_steps: Draw dashed asymptote lines at x=3 and y=−2. Sketch two hyperbola branches.
questions.feedback_wrong: VA: set denominator=0 → x=3. HA: the outside constant → y=−2.

questions.rationale: Formula rearrangement. Kai is 2/2 on this type. New formula: area of circle. One step: divide by π and take √. The distractors test the most common errors.
questions.question_html: The area of a circle is \( A = \pi r^2 \). Which correctly solves for \( r \)?
questions.hint: Isolate r: divide both sides by π, then take the square root.
questions.feedback_wrong: Divide by π first (r²=A/π), THEN take √. Answer: A.

questions.rationale: Exponential DECAY word problem (vs growth in RP4). New context: phone depreciation. Clean answer: t=3 years. Keeps all the same modeling skills (P0, rate factor, period) but tests decay direction. Deliberate switch from RP4 growth scenario to avoid pattern matching.
questions.question_html:
A smartphone originally costs \$800 and loses 25% of its value each year.
(a) Write an exponential model \( V(t) \) for its value after \( t \) years.
(b) After how many years is the phone worth \$337.50?
questions.hint: Decay: V(t) = V₀ · (1 − r)^t. Loses 25% → keeps 75% → decay factor is 0.75.
questions.feedback_correct: Decay model and t=3 years both correct.
questions.feedback_wrong: Decay factor = 0.75 (keeps 75%). Model: V(t)=800·(0.75)^t. Set equal to 337.50 → t=3.
